newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CS sugar output running 7.6 pct up - DataNet.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS sugar output running 7.6 pct up - DataNet.

text.p: Brazilian sugar output in the center-south was 7.6 percent higher by the end of the 15th fortnightly period to December 1 than during the comparative period in 1995/96, said consultants DataNet-Agricommodities.

This is contrast to the 13.18 percent rise seen in figures issued earlier this week by the Sao Paulo Association of Sugar and Alcohol Industries (AIAA) which put output by December 1 at 10.17 million tonnes against 8.98 million by December 1, 1995.
DataNet throughout this season has been comparing results using fortnightly periods rather than dates given the 1996/97 harvest began in mid-April, two weeks earlier than usual.
DataNet also expects the harvest will be shorter than usual and so for comparison purposes is using a moving average to adjust 1995/96 output figures so that the end of harvests will coincide.
Actual sugar production by the end of the 15th period was therefore 10.08 million tonnes against 9.37 million tonnes in 1995/96 using adjusted figures, DataNet said.
Sugar production by the end of the 15th period to December 16 last year was 9.20 million tonnes, according to AIAA figures.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
